entities.name: Platonic Academy
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: Founded by Plato around 387 BCE near Athens, the Academy was the Western world's first institution of higher learning. For nearly 900 years (until Justinian closed it in 529 CE), it taught philosophy, mathematics, and dialectics. It educated Aristotle, shaped Neoplatonism, and established the model of the philosophical school that influenced all subsequent Western universities.
